key_claims: PatchDiff paper: SWE-bench validation runs only tests changed in the linked PR, so patches that break other existing tests count as solved; and many plausible patches behave differently from the gold patch, some certainly wrong. UTBoost: PR-written tests are often insufficient; LLM-generated extra tests find erroneous patches that passed, and a parser bug mislabels more; leaderboard ranks change. OpenAI (snippet only): audit of a subset models often failed found flawed tests rejecting correct solutions, plus contamination; OpenAI stopped reporting Verified. [uncertain for OpenAI]
headline_figures: PatchDiff paper (SWE-bench Verified, 500 tasks, 877 plausible patches: CodeStory 311, LearnByInteract 301, OpenHands 265): 7.8% average of plausible patches fail when all developer tests are run (26/311 8.4%, 23/301 7.6%, 19/265 7.2%); average resolution-rate drop 4.5 points. PatchDiff flags 260/877 (29.6%) as behaviourally different from gold. Of 77 manually analysed (30% sample): 36 (46.8%) divergent implementations, 21 (27.3%) supplementary behaviour, 22 (28.6%) certainly incorrect. Extrapolated 11.0% incorrect among plausible patches; 6.4 absolute points average inflation of resolution rate. (A '6.2' figure in search output was not found in the paper text.) UTBoost: augmented tests flag 170/599 (28.4%) passing Lite patches and 92/584 (15.7%) passing Verified patches as erroneous; insufficient-test instances 23/300 Lite and 26/500 Verified (abstract says 36 total, does not reconcile with 23+26, overlap likely); parser fix changed annotations for 271/500 Verified instances (54.2%) and exposed 79 more erroneous Verified patches; 345 total erroneous (176 Lite + 169 Verified); rank changes 11 of 45 Verified entries (24.4%) and 18 of 44 Lite entries. OpenAI (unverified, snippet): audited a 27.6% subset the models often failed, at least 59.4% of audited problems had flawed tests; progress 74.9% to 80.9% in 6 months. [uncertain]
sample_unit_and_population: PatchDiff: 877 plausible patches from 3 open-source-benchmark agent tools on 500 Verified tasks (open-source Python repos), manual analysis of 77. UTBoost: patches from 45 Verified and 44 Lite leaderboard entries with released patches; only patches passing original tests re-evaluated; tests generated only for instances at least one agent resolved (about 81.6% of Verified).
observed_vs_stated: Observed: code execution of generated tests plus manual review by authors. Not self-report. Both rely on LLM-generated tests (gpt-4o-mini; GPT-4o) and author judgement.
what_makes_trust_justified: Running the full existing test suite, not only PR-modified tests; differential tests between candidate and gold patch; augmenting tests with LLM-generated cases; human review of divergent behaviour. Tests passing alone is weak evidence.
what_it_costs: UTBoost: about $1.6 of API cost per instance for test generation, plus two authors reviewing each flagged case. PatchDiff: LLM calls, up to 2 repair cycles, 20 flakiness reruns per test, plus manual analysis. Human review is the expensive part and was done on samples.
failure_mode_class: Wrong code that passes tests (false pass); benchmark inflation.
control_that_would_have_prevented: Not an incident study. Missing controls: running the full regression suite, differential testing against a reference, stronger or augmented tests, correct log parsing.
limitations_stated: PatchDiff: GPT-4o-mini used for cost; manual bias; 30% sample 'may introduce sampling bias', 9.39% confidence interval at 95%; only flagged patches analysed. UTBoost: tests only for instances some agent resolved; GPT-4o only; simplified Agentless-style generator without tool use; only two authors reviewing.
counter_evidence: Both papers find the incorrect share is a minority (7.8% to 15.7%), so most passing patches were not shown wrong. PatchDiff's divergence flags are not all errors: only 28.6% of sampled flagged patches were certainly incorrect. OpenAI's argument runs the other way (tests reject correct solutions), so tests err in both directions. A later preprint (arXiv 2604.01518) critiques UTBoost's approach; not opened.
verification_status: PatchDiff figures: checked against opened arXiv HTML, but through a summarizing fetch tool, so per-figure wording moderately verified. UTBoost figures: checked against opened abstract and HTML similarly; 36 vs 23+26 discrepancy unresolved. OpenAI figures: NOT verified against primary source [uncertain]. SWE-bench maintainers' own statements: not found or opened [uncertain].
usable_claim: A peer-reviewed study (ICSE 2026) of 877 plausible patches from three agent tools on SWE-bench Verified found that on average 7.8% failed the project's own full developer test suite although they counted as solved, and differential testing flagged 29.6% as behaving differently from the reference fix, of which a manually reviewed sample found 28.6% certainly incorrect. UTBoost (ACL 2025) found that extra generated tests flagged 15.7% (92/584) of passing Verified patches as erroneous.
do_not_use: The OpenAI 59.4% and 27.6% figures and the contamination claims until the primary post is opened. The 6.2-point figure. Any claim that 'a third' or 'a quarter' of Verified solutions are wrong (the 28.6% applies to a sample of flagged patches, not all). The 36-instance total. Adding the 170/92 and 345 figures together.
